Overview
You will be studying Neuroscience in the School of Psychology and Neuroscience where you will be part of a vibrant postgraduate community within a world-class research department lead by internationally recognised academic staff.
Neuroscience is the scientific study of the nervous system, its functions, and its disorders. Neuroscientists use a range of approaches to study the nervous system at different scales, including molecular and cellular studies of individual neurons and glia, electrophysiological recordings of neural activity, brain imaging, behavioural experiments, and clinical studies in patients.
The programme delivers outstanding cutting-edge training, and you will produce new research that significantly advances our understanding in Neuroscience. Our postgraduate students are a central part of the school's research culture and a key component in maintaining our international research reputation.
Key information
Programme duration
MScR: up to two years full-time; up to four years part-time. PhD: up to four years full-time; up to eight years part-time.MD: up to five years full-time; up to eight years part-time.
Start date
January 2027, September 2027, January 2028
Application deadline
Please check our funding webpages for details of funding application deadlines.
Applications from self-funded students are welcomed and have no fixed deadline. However, if you wish to join us in September 2027, please apply with a complete application by 30 June 2027 if you are an overseas student and by 31 July 2027 if you are a home student.

Entry requirements
A first or upper second-class honours degree (or international equivalent) in psychology, neuroscience or a related discipline is required for entry to the PhD and MSc by research programmes.
See international equivalent qualifications on the International Office website.
English language requirements
If English is not your first language, you will need to reach the requirements outlined in our profile level C.
Further information about English language requirements and profile levels.
Fees and funding
Home: full-time
£5,343 per year
Home: part-time
£2,672 per year
Overseas: full-time
£28,300 per year
Fees are subject to an annual review. For programmes that last longer than one year, please budget for up to an 8% increase in fees each year.
More about tuition fees, living costs and financial support.
Alumni discount
University of Bristol students and graduates can benefit from a 25% reduction in tuition fees for postgraduate study. Check your eligibility for an alumni discount.
Funding and scholarships
Further information on funding for prospective UK and international postgraduate students.
Career prospects
Graduates from this programme are well placed to become researchers in universities, research institutes, industry and healthcare. Skills gained from this programme are beneficial in a variety of roles including industry, charities and government.
